purpose: Use the approved Chinese production system as the canonical Tiny Agent longform behavior contract, then produce a natural English localization with the same content, scene grammar, visual system, pacing shape, and cover system; only locale text, locale subtitles, the approved adult English voice, and language-derived absolute timings may differ.

precedence.generationRules: The scheduled-6m18 frozen snapshot supplies the baseline. This active profile is the sole current behavior contract: its fixedBilingualGeneration values and named postSnapshotUserOverrides replace any contradictory snapshot wording. The snapshot files remain immutable evidence and are never copied verbatim into a new project's behavior.
precedence.explicitUserOverrides: A named active override is the only allowed replacement for a contradictory frozen baseline rule. No operational prompt, plan, archive entry, memory note, historical project, or generated QA report may introduce a second behavior rule.
operationalOverlaysAllowed: daily run state machine, recovery, cleanup, and deduplication
current cover deliverables and deterministic cover text
current Tiny Agent asset manifest integrity
fixed bilingual outro copy and alignment
English Postiz publication and public playlist verification
precedence.forbiddenBlending: Rules introduced after the 2026-07-23 03:02-04:17 scheduled run may not alter a generation dimension covered by the frozen snapshot. In particular, do not blend in the later V4 +10 percent rates, 9-12 minute target, one-story requirement, three-module limit, recap removal, 35-45-state target, opening glyph lead, complete-question hold, or later motion choreography, except where an explicit active postSnapshotUserOverrides rule names a narrower replacement.

englishChineseProductionParity.rule: Chinese is the canonical production grammar. Author and approve the shared content contract and Chinese scene system first, then localize that exact semantic and visual plan into natural English. English may not introduce a different hook concept, content claim, chapter, example, reusable artifact, scene type, layout family, role/prop assignment, generated-art semantic, motion type, transition grammar, caption treatment, chapter rail, recap layout, outro layout, or cover geometry. Do not mechanically translate wording and do not reuse Chinese timestamps; preserve meaning and production form while deriving English wording and absolute timing from final English TTS/VTT.
allowedDifferences: natural locale text, subtitles, and locale metadata
absolute cue, scene, and animation timestamps derived independently from each locale's final TTS/VTT
English YouTube delivery uses a 3840x2160 16:9 master while Chinese local delivery retains its required 1280x720, 1200x900, and 900x1200 files

content.rule: Both locale projects must contain byte-identical bilingual-content-contract.json files. The contract maps the source, thesis, priorities, chapter IDs, scene IDs, recap IDs, examples, caveats, and reusable artifact before either localized script is approved. Every required review flag is true. Localized content-map.json and scene-plan.json files must reference the same contractId.

sceneStructure.rule: English and Chinese must use the same chapter count, scene count, recap count, generated-art scene positions, scene IDs/order, layout sequence, roles, props, semantic motion sequence, transition grammar, and outro position. Only localized copy and final-VTT-derived absolute timing fields may differ.

pacing.rule: Compare pacing after normalizing each locale to its own final duration. English may breathe naturally, but its chapter and scene duration shares must stay within the declared differences from Chinese. A different language is not permission to create a differently paced edit.

cover16x9.rule: The English 16:9 cover is a language-localized rendering of the Chinese 16:9 cover system, not a separate YouTube art direction. At the 1280x720 SVG design coordinate system, both locales use the exact paper grid, blue rule, title zone, hero box, and yellow rule above. The title may reflow naturally inside the same zone; the semantic title, one complete current-topic Tiny Agent action, colors, and hierarchy remain aligned. Only the English 4K publication raster size differs.
cover16x9.qa: The bilingual parity validator must parse both final 16:9 SVGs and their specs, verify this geometryProfileId, compare the actual grid/rules/title zone/hero box against the active profile, and reject any normalized geometry or cover-semantic mismatch.

qa.rule: Run the bilingual parity validator after both locale projects have final content maps, scripts, TTS/VTT-derived scene and animation plans, metadata, and 16:9 covers. It writes the same hash-bound report to both projects. Each per-project output validator must reject a missing, stale, failing, or wrong-pair report before render or publication.

chapterRecapNarration.purpose: Retain the spoken three-point recap structure, restore the blue chapter-recap sidebar, and render a numbered left-aligned three-point body.

screenCopy.rule: Every recap scene must carry two independently authored values: narration preserves the locale's required spoken recap and ordinal prefix; recapDisplayText contains only the concise substantive claim, not narration or headline. Render a blue left sidebar containing the chapter-recap label and that chapter's title. Render the three substantive body points left-aligned from recapDisplayText, with visible blue Arabic-dot labels 1., 2., 3. in a dedicated number column. Do not place spoken ordinal words inside recapDisplayText or the substantive claim text. On-screen subtitles are a faithful final-VTT transcript and may show the spoken recap and ordinal prefixes.
screenCopy.zh-CN: The sidebar shows 第 N 章小节 and the current chapter title. The three visible body rows are left-aligned and show blue 1.、2.、3. labels beside claims stripped of their spoken prefixes. Captions retain the final VTT, including 本章小节、第一、第二、第三.
screenCopy.en-US: The sidebar shows Chapter N recap and the current chapter title. The three visible body rows are left-aligned and show blue 1., 2., 3. labels beside claims stripped of their spoken prefixes. Captions retain the final VTT, including Chapter recap, First, Second, and Third.

chapterRecapNarration.qa: Generate qa/recap-visual-copy-report.json with pass=true, renderedMarkerScanPass=true, and one recaps[] entry per scene containing sceneId, narration, recapDisplayText, sidebar, visibleBodyNumbers, bodyTextAlignment=left, bodyUsesOnlyRecapDisplayText=true, forbiddenMarkerCount=0, and numberedBulletPresent=true. Confirm the required narration prefixes, the blue sidebar and chapter title, cumulative visible 1./2./3. labels, left-aligned substantive body copy, and final-VTT captions. Fail production on any mismatch.

openingQuestionReadability.purpose: Make the opening question immediately arresting and comfortably readable while keeping the measured final VTT as the timing authority.

spokenBridge.rule: To give the viewer time to read the complete visible question, the opening utterance may end with one short, natural, non-displayed spoken bridge after the literal visible-question VTT prefix. The bridge is part of the final opening VTT and audio, never a frozen hold. The visible question must remain an exact ordered prefix of that VTT; its final glyph must settle 40-180ms before the literal question cue ends, then remain completely readable for 1100-1650ms before the opening utterance audible end while the bridge is spoken.

compactTextBlock.purpose: Treat the opening question as actual visible text mass, not a tall outer box. Sum final-font glyph-row heights and permit only the measured adjacent line gaps. Never spread two lines into distant bands or count a blank interline area toward coverage.
compactTextBlock.layout: Use the largest safe semantic 2-4-line stack. If two lines cannot meet the glyph-mass height and width targets while clearing the Agent, add a semantic line instead of inserting vertical whitespace. Consecutive final glyph rows must remain within maxInterlineGapPx.
compactTextBlock.qa: qa/retention-opening-report.json must record final-font per-line glyph bounds, consecutive interline gaps, glyphMassHeightPercent, and compactTextBlockPass. Fail when a gap exceeds maxInterlineGapPx, the line count is outside semanticLineCount, or glyph-mass height is outside glyphMassHeightPercent.

uniformAdaptiveTypography.layout: Use the bundled ordinary Hiragino Sans GB UI sans for both locales, not a locale-specific display face. Compute one largest safe final font size for the complete opening stack. Every visible question line in that locale uses that exact font size; English may choose different natural line breaks, but may not use mixed per-line sizes or a different type system. When the Agent box or a canvas edge constrains the stack, reduce the single shared size for every line together.

accentTokenContract.rule: Each locale declares natural, topic-specific openingAccentTokens in episode.json. Both must include the AI Agent identity, the same concrete topic concept, and the same risk/action concept in that locale; never retain keywords from a previous episode.

uniformAdaptiveTypography.qa: qa/retention-opening-report.json must record final computed font family, font weight, every line font size, uniformFontSizePass, accent runs, and accentTokenPass. Fail when active scoped opening lines do not use one exact final size, the embedded font contract is missing, topic-specific episode.openingAccentTokens are missing, a configured keyword accent is absent or uses the wrong tone, or the English and Chinese openings use different typography systems.

openingQuestionReadability.layout: After final-font layout, use semantic 2-4-line breaks and the largest safe type. Actual first-question text mass must occupy 64%-92% of canvas width and 86%-94% of canvas height under compactTextBlock; its compact outer bounds must occupy 90%-98% of canvas height. Empty space between remote line bands never counts as text: whenever a safe area remains, enlarge the adjacent glyphs before considering another line. In any locale covered by uniformAdaptiveTypography, all question lines use its one shared adaptive size. Reserve the lower-right agent box named by agentReservation: the question may use the rest of the canvas but may not overlap the Agent, question mark, emphasis marks, or outer safe margin. No opening glyph, punctuation, Agent, or accent may clip or overflow.
openingQuestionReadability.timing: The first glyph/word becomes visible 120-180 milliseconds before the final VTT audible onset. Every later visible unit must also begin 120-180 milliseconds before its own VTT-derived audible onset; a declared maximum is not proof. Derive and record each unit's audible onset from the literal visible-question cue, compare it with the actual timeline start, and fail closed unless every measured lead is in range. The final visible-question glyph must settle 40-180 milliseconds before the literal question cue ends, then remain fully readable 1100-1650 milliseconds before the opening-utterance audible end, using only the permitted spokenBridge when needed. Hard-cut directly to the body at the measured speech boundary; do not add a static hold after the speech ends.
openingQuestionReadability.zh-CN: Reveal each Han character and punctuation in order. Each character and punctuation must begin 120-180ms before its own VTT-derived audible onset, then settle before the literal question cue ends; do not reveal unrelated future characters.
openingQuestionReadability.en-US: Reveal words in speaking order, with letters resolving quickly within each word. Every visible word must begin 120-180ms before its own VTT-derived audible onset and settle before the literal question cue ends; do not reveal unrelated future phrases.
openingQuestionReadability.agent: The approved Tiny Agent is fully visible in the lower-right reserved box from the very first rendered opening frame. It has no delayed entrance, opacity fade-in, or reveal animation.

regularGlyph.settledPose: Every glyph must finish at x=0, y=0, rotation=0, scale=1. The ordered VTT-derived reveal schedule remains authoritative; direction changes may not reveal a later glyph early.

finalQuestionGlyph.settledPose: The red question mark finishes upright at x=0, y=0, rotation=0, scale=1.12, with questionMarkGapPx clear space from the preceding glyph.

kineticGlyphEntrance.purpose: Use a deterministic four-direction kinetic entrance for the opening text: each ordered glyph travels in from a different diagonal direction, then settles cleanly into the final readable layout. Do not use random motion, a fade-only reveal, or a delayed Agent entrance.

hookQuestionQuality.purpose: Make the first visible question earn attention by directly naming the episode's concrete task/topic and opening a useful unknown or viewer benefit. It must invite the viewer to understand causes, mechanisms, trade-offs, triggers, or an actionable path; it must never replace the actual topic with an unrelated long-task, drift, memory, handoff, or other scenario, and it must never spend the opening on an obvious yes-or-no proposition whose answer is already common knowledge to the intended audience.
forbiddenQuestionForms: restatement of a commonly known problem as a question
question whose visible wording already supplies its own answer
tangential scenario or pain point that the episode does not actually teach
hookQuestionQuality.authoring: Start from what the episode actually teaches, not from a reusable dramatic template. Name the concrete task/topic in the question and ask the shortest natural causal, mechanism, trade-off, trigger, or actionable-path question that exposes its value. For an episode about writing an AI Agent Skill, ask directly how to write or design a useful reusable Skill; do not introduce long tasks or drift unless the episode itself teaches those topics.
hookQuestionQuality.semanticLineBreak: Keep the AI Agent identity and the concrete task/topic intact. When a Chinese causal marker such as 为什么、如何 or 怎么 begins the interrogative clause, keep the causal clause together as a compact adjacent lower stack; if it needs two lines to reach the required glyph mass, break only between whole Chinese words and never separate the causal marker from its immediate predicate.
hookQuestionQuality.qa: Before rendering, write qa/opening-hook-quality-report.json. It must record the exact visibleQuestion, one or more directTopicTerms that include a concrete episode topic beyond the generic AI Agent identity, the viewerValue, the audiencePainPoint, the knowledgeGap, the topicAlignmentRationale, tangentialSetupRisk, the rejectedObviousQuestion, the selected allowed intent, and measured checks for directEpisodeTopic, viewerValueOrCuriosity, and noTangentialScenarioSetup. pass=true only when the question directly asks about the actual episode topic, makes its value or knowledge gap clear, uses an allowed intent, creates unresolved curiosity, and is not tangential, obvious yes-or-no, or self-answering. The longform output validator must fail closed when this evidence is missing, generic, or does not match the final VTT hook.

openingQuestionReadability.openingUi: The opening contains no dedicated progress rail, blue circular progress marker, or VOICE label. Delete those elements from the opening DOM and timeline; the normal chapter progress may begin only after the opening hard cut.
openingQuestionReadability.qa: Generate qa/retention-opening-report.json from final VTT, final-font DOM measurement, and rendered first-frame inspection. Record each visible unit's VTT-derived audible onset, actual visual start, measured perGlyphAudibleLeadMilliseconds, literalQuestionCompletionLeadMilliseconds, firstGlyphLeadMilliseconds, fullQuestionReadLeadMilliseconds, canvas glyph coverage, Agent first-frame visibility and bounds, hard-cut time, and an opening-ui absence scan. Fail if any unit lead is outside the active perGlyphAudibleLeadMilliseconds range, the final unit does not settle before the literal question cue ends, any value is outside this profile, the Agent is absent at frame zero, a forbidden opening UI element is present, or any opening element clips, overlaps, or exceeds its safe area.

generatedArtTransparency.purpose: Keep temporary generated-art scenes visually native to the shared paper-grid composition.
generatedArtTransparency.deliveryAsset: Every temporary generated-art asset actually referenced by a scene must be a PNG or WebP with a real alpha channel. Its four corner pixels must be fully transparent and it must contain no opaque, full-canvas, solid-color, gradient, paper, panel, or grid background.
generatedArtTransparency.generationAndCleanup: Request a transparent background at generation time. If a generation tool cannot emit alpha, remove the temporary key/flat background deterministically before composition; a backgrounded source is never an acceptable delivered scene asset.
generatedArtTransparency.composition: Place only the isolated subject directly over the video composition's existing paper-grid background. Do not add a source-image background plate, opaque wrapper, or replacement grid behind it.
generatedArtTransparency.qa: Generate qa/generated-art-alpha-report.json with pass=true, sharedGridComposition=true, and one assets[] entry per referenced temporary generated-art file. Each entry records file, hasAlpha=true, four cornerAlpha values of 0, canvasEdgeBackgroundDetected=false, opaque-bounds versus canvas bounds, and sceneIds. Fail if any file lacks alpha, has a non-transparent corner, retains a canvas-edge background, or is not composed directly over the shared grid.

englishAdultNarration.selection: Use the mainstream adult US-English Christopher voice: news/narration oriented, reliable and authoritative. It is the only permitted English longform narrator.
englishAdultNarration.purpose: Use a clearly adult, reliable, authoritative English narration instead of the former cute/conversational voice.
englishAdultNarration.qa: The final English episode.json, summary.json, timing-map.json, TTS command evidence, and speech-pacing report must all name en-US-ChristopherNeural at +30%. Reject en-US-AnaNeural and every other English longform voice.

chinesePronunciation.purpose: Make every viewer-facing Chinese narration use the intended reading of content-bearing polyphonic terms. A visually correct Chinese script is not sufficient when its TTS reading is ambiguous or wrong.
chinesePronunciation.authoring: Before TTS, identify every content-bearing polyphonic term whose reading can change the meaning in the final Chinese narration. For each such term, record the intended Hanyu Pinyin and choose a natural spoken phrase that makes that reading unambiguous to zh-CN-YunxiaNeural. Prefer a lexical rewrite or a grammatical context that preserves the meaning, for example use 长期任务 for a long-duration task instead of submitting the ambiguous bare phrase 长任务. Never put raw pinyin, parenthetical pronunciation notes, markup, or a spelling-out instruction into viewer-visible narration or captions.
chinesePronunciation.evidence: episode.json must contain chinesePronunciationReview.entries[]. Each entry records ambiguousForm, intendedPinyin, approvedTtsText, strategy, and the final TTS segmentIds that use it. The approvedTtsText must be a natural phrase in the final script/VTT; the ambiguousForm must not be sent as the unqualified TTS phrase when a safer equivalent is used.
chinesePronunciation.qa: Before rendering any Chinese project, generate qa/chinese-pronunciation-report.json from the final TTS segments. It must record pass=true only after every declared term has intendedPinyin, an approved natural TTS phrase, matching final segment evidence, and a deliberate lexical or grammatical disambiguation. The longform output validator must fail closed if this report is absent, stale, or incomplete. The reviewer must audition the opening and any changed pronunciation before approving a review render or a master.

chineseMandarinProsody.purpose: Make Chinese narration and its readable subtitle timing follow natural Putonghua thought groups, rather than cutting at arbitrary written fragments.
chineseMandarinProsody.authoring: Write the final Chinese script in complete natural sentences. Mark an intended ordinary pause with Chinese punctuation inside the sentence, and make punctuation, phrase order, and named entities readable by zh-CN-YunxiaNeural. Do not use a comma, enumeration comma, colon, or semicolon as an artificial TTS-segment boundary; preserve it inside the complete sentence so the voice can make the ordinary brief pause. Do not begin a sentence with continuation punctuation or leave a sentence as a dangling modifier, connector, or half clause.

ttsSegmentation.rule: Each Chinese TTS segment must be one complete sentence ending in a configured sentence terminator. Internal commas, enumeration commas, colons, and semicolons remain within that segment. Never split the audio merely because a visual scene, card, or caption changes.

captions.partialSentenceException: Only the final bottom VTT caption may be a partial spoken sentence. It must stay contiguous with the narration and, when a long cue must split, use a natural Mandarin punctuation boundary; it may never be copied into a headline, card, prop label, yellow highlight, chapter panel, recap, or outro.
captions.rule: Keep final VTT cue order and wording faithful to the final audio. Do not create a cue that begins with continuation punctuation or ends in an unclosed quotation, bracket, or dangling punctuation fragment.

chineseMandarinProsody.qa: Before rendering a Chinese project, generate qa/chinese-mandarin-prosody-report.json from the final TTS segment list and final narration VTT. Record every segment and cue, its boundary punctuation, and its pass. Fail production when a segment ends at forbidden boundary punctuation, lacks a complete sentence terminator, begins with continuation punctuation, is not contiguous with final script text, or when a caption cue has an invalid natural-pause boundary. The output validator must reject a missing, stale, or failing report.

onScreenTextCompleteness.purpose: Ensure every visible non-caption text unit is a finished reader-facing thought, not a clipped prefix copied from the narration.
onScreenTextCompleteness.captionsOnlyException: Only final bottom VTT captions may show a partial spoken sentence. Captions are not visual-summary copy and must remain subject to the Mandarin/locale caption rule.
onScreenTextCompleteness.authoring: Independently author every scene headline, object or prop label, authority card, yellow highlight, chapter intro, recap body, promise copy, and outro as a complete sentence, question, imperative, or concise self-contained noun phrase. Never take an arbitrary leading slice of narration, leave a dangling punctuation or clause, or use line wrapping to hide an incomplete thought. If an authority/source name is visible, take it from the current episode's source attribution and never hard-code an unrelated product or publisher.
onScreenTextCompleteness.qa: Before rendering, generate qa/on-screen-text-completeness-report.json from the final scene plan and rendered DOM. Include every non-caption visible text unit with its id, kind, text, source binding, narration comparison, and pass. Reject a strict narration-prefix fragment, dangling terminal punctuation or unmatched quotation/bracket, absent source-backed authority label, a rendered-DOM/report mismatch, or any failing unit. The longform output validator must fail closed when this report is missing, stale, or failing.

coverPrimaryTitleOnly.rule: A cover may contain only its deterministic primary title. Auxiliary short phrases, subtitles, taglines, benefit copy, chapter labels, CTA text, and explanatory microcopy are forbidden.
coverPrimaryTitleOnly.qa: Fail cover QA when any text other than the approved primary title is present.

coverTitleTopicAlignment.rule: Every cover primary title must be a concise, natural expression of the same concrete topic as its local publishing title. Before cover authoring, declare a per-episode `coverTitleContract` in that locale's `publish-metadata.<locale>.json`: its core cover keywords, the title-term equivalents that prove each keyword is present in the publishing title, and the concrete topic action shown by the hero. Every normal delivered cover headline must contain every declared core cover keyword literally; choose the words that state the episode's actual pain point or action, not a vague slogan. For the current Chinese long-running-agent episode, the required literal cover keywords are `长任务` and `交接`, while `长期任务` is the approved publishing-title equivalent of `长任务`. The English counterpart uses the same intent: the English cover must carry the episode's concrete long-running-task and handoff keywords, not a detached generic Agent slogan.

zhRatioTitleInformationDensity.rule: Chinese 4:3 and 3:4 covers must carry a complete topic question, action, or benefit, not only an identity plus a bare topic noun such as AI Agent Skill. Match the approved prior-cover density: after removing the AI Agent identity, the primary title retains at least minimumInformationUnitsBeyondIdentity meaningful Han glyphs or alphanumeric words, uses titleLineCount large title lines, and fills at least the ratio-specific minimumTitleBlockHeightPercent of the canvas. This remains one primary title, not auxiliary copy.
zhRatioTitleInformationDensity.qa: The Chinese cover-reference validator must measure the final SVG headline, line count, title-block height, information units beyond the AI Agent identity, and question/action/benefit intent. Fail 4:3 or 3:4 when any density value is below this active contract, even if the core cover keywords are present.

coverTitleTopicAlignment.qa: Run `validate-tiny-agent-zh-cover-reference.mjs` for zh-CN and `validate-tiny-agent-en-cover-reference.mjs` for en-US. They must reject a missing or malformed coverTitleContract, a publishing title that does not contain an approved equivalent for every core cover keyword, a normal delivered cover that omits a required keyword, or a cover whose generated hero action differs from the declared topic action. A ratio may omit a newly introduced keyword only when its spec records a concrete owner-requested revision-scope exemption; the exemption is not a reusable production rule.

coverReferenceAlignment.layout: Use the reference title-hero system: neutral paper-grid background; a short blue rule at the top; title-led left/top zone; one complete Tiny Agent plus one topic object; and a single yellow rule at the bottom or the portrait 60/40 divider. The yellow rule is decorative only and never underlines title text.

zhRatioStrictGeometry.rule: Chinese 4:3 and 3:4 covers must use the approved deterministic SVG geometry above exactly: the paper grid, rounded blue and yellow rules, four title baselines, title group styling, and ratio-specific hero box are fixed. Only the episode title text, content-fitted font sizes within the declared range, and the current-topic transparent hero asset may change. Do not stretch the 4:3 yellow rule across the canvas, remove rounded ends, reduce the title to a high empty-space block, or move the portrait divider away from y=0.60H.
zhRatioStrictGeometry.qa: The Chinese cover-reference validator must parse the final SVG and fail closed unless every scoped grid, rule, title-group, four-line baseline, dominant body-line size, hero-box, preview dimension, and strictGeometryProfileId value matches this geometry contract with zero pixel tolerance. A semantic-density pass alone is never sufficient.

coverReferenceAlignment.titleColors: Use exactly two title colors: #117ABD only for the AI Agent identity phrase, and #111413 for every remaining title glyph. #F4C542 is reserved for the decorative rule; #8A6500 and #C7362F are forbidden in title text.
coverReferenceAlignment.character: For every Chinese episode, the 4:3 right-side hero and 3:4 lower hero must each be newly generated as a temporary, current-topic illustration; for every English episode, the delivered 16:9 hero must likewise be newly generated as a temporary, current-topic illustration. Do not reuse a previous episode's hero, a stable Agent-plus-prop pairing, or a decorative prop. Each generated hero may include exactly one complete Tiny Agent only, preserve the approved white rounded body, black face screen, blue eyes and antenna, brown tool belt, and hand-drawn outline, and actively perform the `coverTitleContract` concrete topic action with its integrated topic object. It never permits a second character, collage, generated text, or an unrelated decorative prop. A ratio may remain in the older reference system only when its own spec records a concrete owner-requested revision-scope exemption; the exemption is not a reusable production rule.
coverReferenceAlignment.qa: Before approval, compare all ratios against the reference title-hero system and verify the blue rule, blue-plus-black title hierarchy, bottom yellow rule, one complete Tiny Agent, one complete topic action, no title underline, no auxiliary copy, and no generated text. Every normal zh-CN 4:3/3:4 SVG and every normal en-US 16:9 SVG must reference exactly one current-episode alpha PNG generated for that ratio, with a verified transparent corner; its ratio spec must record `characterCount=1`, the required Tiny Agent identity anchors, an integrated topic action matching `coverTitleContract`, chroma-key alpha removal, and `generatedIllustrationText=false`. Chinese 4:3/3:4 must additionally pass `zhRatioStrictGeometry`; semantic title density cannot substitute for exact geometry. Run the locale's cover-reference validator and fail the run on any ratio mismatch.

publishingMetadata.titleIdentity: Every platform/local metadata title, in-video topic title, and cover title must naturally identify AI Agent(s) or 智能体 and state the concrete topic, question, action, or benefit. Prefer the literal AI Agent wording whenever it reads naturally; never use a detached slogan that loses the Agent topic. Grammar must also assign every action to its real actor: when a person writes, creates, designs, or turns work into a Skill for an AI Agent, the title must make the person/viewer the implied actor and the AI Agent the target or user, not falsely make the Agent the author.

titleSemanticAgency.rule: A title must preserve semantic agency from the source and script. Human-authored work uses a human/viewer construction such as 如何为 AI Agent 写出真正可复用的 Skill or How to write a reusable Skill for an AI Agent. Do not write AI Agent 怎样把一次好结果变成可复用 Skill or an equivalent Agent-as-author construction when the episode actually teaches the viewer to perform that transformation. An Agent may be the grammatical actor only when the cited source and episode explicitly teach the Agent performing that action autonomously.
titleSemanticAgency.qa: The title-identity report must record hasAccurateAgency for every checked title and fail closed on a common Agent-as-author construction for human-authored Skill creation. Human review must also compare the publishing title with the episode's actual actor, action, target, and benefit before approval.

publishingMetadata.description: Put the episode keyword and viewer benefit in the first two lines. Include exactly three topic-specific learning gains, then finish the final non-hashtag line with the locale's fixed follow sentence. Do not include source blocks, source-title stitching, or external links.

zh-CN.fixedFollowSentence: 关注 Tiny Agent，成为更擅长使用 AI 的人！

en-US.fixedFollowSentence: Follow Tiny Agent. Tiny Agent helps you get better at using AI.

publishingMetadata.qa: Run the title-identity metadata validator. It must reject a title without Agent identity, concrete context, or accurate semantic agency, and reject a description whose final non-hashtag line is not the locale's fixed follow sentence.

fixedBilingualGeneration.chapterPattern: chapter opening, body, and spoken three-point recap
fixedBilingualGeneration.opening: voice-synced kinetic question using the active readable-full-question coverage and accelerated completion override; no extended later-V4 hold
fixedBilingualGeneration.visualReference: 63 scenes, 7 chapters, 15 recap scenes, 15.873 percent temporary generated scenes, 7 motion types, and 29 motion beats in the Chinese reference implementation
